children: Luxury companies are expected to report a slowdown in demand despite likely better trends in September, BofA analysts write in a research note. The third quarter will likely show that the downturn was primarily in July and the first two weeks of August, the analysts say, noting that things should look less bad from mid-August. Chinese demand remained soft during summer and "there continues to be limited evidence of green shoots necessary for a material recovery, with consumer confidence remaining low," they add. U.S. demand could have moderated, while in Europe tourism remains a drag, BofA says. (andrea.figueras@wsj.com)
